subtopic: KV cache dataflow / Layout and bandwidth
learningObjective: Reason about the KV cache dataflow during a single autoregressive decode step and its interaction with attention kernels.
stem: Consider one decode step for a batch of B sequences, each of length seq_len (varying). Select all correct statements about KV-cache dataflow inside a single attention layer. (Choose all that apply.)

options.text: The step writes exactly one new K entry and one new V entry per sequence (each of size H_kv * d), then reads the full cache of length seq_len for each sequence to compute attention. Write traffic is small; read traffic is dominated by seq_len.

KV cache must be stored in one contiguous [B, H_kv, MAX_SEQ, d] tensor per layer to enable coalesced reads by the attention kernel; PagedAttention breaks this requirement and therefore has strictly higher HBM latency per attention step.

In MQA/GQA the same K, V pair is read by multiple query heads within a token; a well-designed attention kernel keeps the loaded K/V tile in SMEM and reuses it across query heads, avoiding redundant HBM reads.

Because decode is memory-bandwidth bound on KV reads, KV cache quantization (e.g., FP8 or INT8 KV) is a direct lever on decode latency, subject to available dequant kernels and acceptable accuracy loss.

explanation: A is correct: canonical read/write pattern. C is correct: MQA/GQA lets one KV tile serve multiple Q heads, and good kernels exploit this reuse in SMEM. D is correct: decode is bandwidth-bound on KV, so cutting KV bytes directly cuts wall time. B is wrong: PagedAttention uses a block-table indirection but delivers the loaded blocks to the attention kernel in tiles just like the contiguous layout would; measured HBM latency is not intrinsically higher (the paged layout adds indirection cost but avoids fragmentation cost).

optionExplanations.C: Correct: MQA/GQA KV reuse across Q heads.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: KV quant is a direct bandwidth lever.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: paged layout is not intrinsically slower per step; it addresses fragmentation.

assumptions: Sequences of varying length are handled either as a batched-with-mask kernel or via a paged attention kernel.
nonImplications: Does not imply PagedAttention has zero overhead; there is a small indirection cost.
Does not imply KV quantization is free; it needs kernels and adds accuracy risk.

distractorRationales.B: Overstates paged overhead; ignores fragmentation benefits.
